1 Overview and glossary

1.1 What the system is

Spice Town is a South Asian grocery, halal meat and prepared-food store in Vernon, CT that sells through Toast POS / Toast Retail. This system is the store's own operations platform. It reads everything the store sells from Toast, keeps a day-by-day copy of the inventory, and works out what to order, from whom and how much. It also runs the store's paperwork and team work: purchase orders, deliveries, invoices, inventory clean-up (Fix Issues), daily checklists, team tasks, chat, announcements, marketing flyers, push notifications and sales insights.

There are three ways in, all served by one FastAPI process on one Mac mini in the store's office:

  • Website (React single-page app) at https://ops.spicetown.shop, signed in with an httpOnly session cookie. Admins use it for setup and for the larger pages.
  • Mobile app (Flutter, iOS and Android, bundle com.spicetown.app, version 2.0.0+8), signed in with a bearer token kept in the Keychain / Keystore, optionally unlocked with Face ID. Five tabs: Home, Store, Scan, Team, More.
  • Public checklist links (/c/<slug>-<code>) for part-time staff without an account: one checklist form, no login, heavily rate limited.

A separate labels app (Flask, labels.spicetown.shop) prints shelf labels on a Brother QL-810W. It shares the dashboard's login by reading the dashboard's user_sessions table read-only. Nothing in this system writes to Toast: every Toast call is a read (the API scopes granted have no write and no purchasing access).

1.4 Glossary

TermMeaning
Business dateToast's store day. The store's day closes out at 04:00 America/New_York; jobs that need yesterday's final numbers run after 04:00.
Selection / modifierOne line item on a Toast check (a selection). A modifier (spice level, add-on) is itself a selection nested under its parent; stored with parent_selection_guid. 'Real sold items' always filter parent_selection_guid IS NULL.
Inventory snapshotOne row per item per day in inventory_snapshots, from the Toast 'retail items' CSV/XLSX upload or (when switched on) built from the Toast API at 04:05. snapshot_date D holds the opening count of day D.
Container rowA second bare row of the same item tracking stock kept in the storage container; paired with the priced store row (store_container_pairs).
Supplier / vendorFree text from Toast's supplier field; can list several vendors separated by ';'.
Reorder candidate / tierAn item whose forecast demand over the vendor lead time is above on-hand. Vendors are grouped with an urgency tier (critical, soon, ...).
Critical vendorA vendor with at least one critical item; shown on Home's red Critical tile and in the Morning summary. Admins can Close / Skip this week / Remind me later (critical_vendor_dismissals).
Supplier Projection ('New order')Per-vendor demand projection with an availability-adjusted forecast and a suggested order quantity.
Order dueA date on the Vendor Calendar when an order must be placed for the next delivery (from vendor_schedules weekday + lead days).
PO cartOne shared store cart of purchase-order lines (po_cart_items), grouped by vendor and by PO section.
PO sectionThe aisle-like heading a product prints under on the vendor PO PDF (automatic from category, editable with po_section_rules).
Placed orderA row in placed_orders: an order sent or recorded (status pdf / placed; source cart / outside / sent).
Fix IssuesInventory-hygiene lists (missing / invalid barcodes, duplicates, dead stock, slow review, negative, refill) that staff close with a reason.
Lead / lead taskThe person responsible for a PO section or vendor's Fix Issues items; each lead gets one daily Team task, titled 'Fix Issues: N left of M'.
Team change feedteam_changes: every Team write appends a row; clients ask GET /api/team/updates?since=<cursor> for what changed.
Long-pollGET /api/team/updates with wait=1..20: the server holds the request until something the caller can see changes, or the wait ends.
Feature keyOne of 20 admin-grantable access keys (features.py). Admins have every key.
hide_salesPer-user flag: no dollar figures, no Items Sold, no sales-only Insights.
can_assignPer-user flag: a non-admin may assign tasks to other people.
Demo loginThe App Review account (app_store_review, users.id 8): sees what its features allow, may only write to its own sandbox; nothing it does leaves the server.
Morning summaryOne 09:00 push per admin listing critical vendors, orders due, loss watch, Fix Issues items back, inventory upload, yesterday's sales and open checks.
Quiet hours22:00-07:00 store time: scheduled alerts are not sent.
Store defaultsAdmin-set default on/off per alert per role (staff / admin), stored in setting_changes; a person's own choice always wins.
Report cacheIn-process cache for the heavy Today report and Vendor Calendar counts (Oct 15), cleared by any committed write to the tables they read.
ERAToast's Analytics API ('enterprise reporting'): a report is requested (POST) and fetched later (GET) - two steps.
WhapiThe WhatsApp Business gateway used to post to the store's WhatsApp groups (plan: sandbox, 5 chats).

2 Deployment topology

2.1 Host and daemons

Everything runs on one always-on Mac mini (hostname spicetown-server) in the store. Services are macOS LaunchDaemons in /Library/LaunchDaemons/ (they run without anyone logged in), each with RunAtLoad + KeepAlive. There is no crontab, no container and no second server.

launchd labelProgramNotes
com.spicetown.backend~/spicetown-backend/backend/.venv312/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000API + website + 3 schedulers + flyer sender. ONE process, never --workers (caches, locks and the task long-poll are in-process). stdout logs/backend.log, stderr logs/backend.error.log. The repo copy of the plist still names .venv (py3.9); the installed one uses .venv312.
com.spicetown.cloudflared/opt/homebrew/bin/cloudflared tunnel run spicetown-opsIngress (~/.cloudflared/config.yml): ops.spicetown.shop -> :8000, labels.spicetown.shop -> :8080, flowers.spicetown.shop -> :8085, anything else 404.
com.spicetown.cloudflared.updaterbackend/scripts/update_cloudflared.shDaily 04:30; restarts the tunnel only when the version changed.
com.spicetown.watchdogbackend/scripts/watchdog.sh (root)Every 300 s; re-bootstraps backend, cloudflared, labels if not loaded. Not flowers or labels.sync.
com.spicetown.labelsspicetown-labels/scripts/run_gunicorn.shSeparate repo, venv and SQLite DB. Prints over CUPS.
com.spicetown.labels.syncspicetown-labels/scripts/sync_catalog.shEvery 15 min: git pull the catalog CSV (built by a GitHub Action from Toast), POST /api/refresh.
com.spicetown.flowersspicetown-flowers/site/serve.pyUnrelated static site sharing the tunnel.

2.2 Inside the backend process

One uvicorn process runs one FastAPI app. Async handlers (the change-feed long-poll) run on the event loop; ordinary def handlers run in Starlette's thread pool. Three APScheduler BackgroundSchedulers and a few daemon threads live in the same process and share its CPU, GIL and SQLite connection pool.

  • Lifespan (main.py): start main scheduler, notification scheduler, team scheduler, flyer sender; stop in reverse on shutdown.
  • App-wide dependency demo_write_guard runs for every route, including ones added later (section 3.5).
  • Routers: 34 router objects included in a fixed order; the public checklist page router is registered before the static mount at /.
  • Exception handler: a 401/403 on /public/invoices/* becomes a 302 to /#/login?next=... so a WhatsApp link opens the login page instead of JSON.
  • SQLite (app/db.py): WAL journal, busy_timeout=5000, and (Oct 15) per-connection cache_size=-16384 (16 MB), mmap_size=256 MB, temp_store=MEMORY. The UTCDateTime column type re-attaches UTC on read (SQLite drops it).

2.3 Network exposure and domains

  • Cloudflare Tunnel: cloudflared keeps an outbound connection to Cloudflare; Cloudflare terminates TLS. No port forwarding, no public IP. Domains: ops.spicetown.shop (this system), labels.spicetown.shop, flowers.spicetown.shop.
  • Session cookie domain is .spicetown.shop in production (SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN), so the labels subdomain receives the same cookie and can check the dashboard login.
  • CORS: CORS_ORIGINS (dev Vite origin and leftovers of the retired Capacitor wrapper), credentials allowed. The website is same-origin in production, so CORS matters only for dev.
  • PUBLIC_BASE_URL = https://ops.spicetown.shop in production; used to build invoice links and public checklist links. (Its code default still names the old Tailscale host.)
  • Tailscale is dev-only now: up.sh starts a dev uvicorn on :8001 (with --reload, DB spicetown-dev.db, schedulers off) and tailscale serve --https=8443 exposes it to the tailnet for phone testing.

2.4 How the website is served

  • npm run build writes frontend/dist; FastAPI mounts it at / with StaticFiles(html=True) (one process, one port).
  • index.html is sent with Cache-Control: no-cache; hashed assets with public, max-age=86400. A new build is live on the next page load - no restart for website-only changes.
  • The website uses HashRouter (/#/reorder), so no server-side catch-all route is needed.
  • /c/<slug>-<code> is a FastAPI route that returns the same index.html with a strict CSP; main.jsx renders only the public checklist page for /c/ paths.

2.5 Deploy flow and rollback

  • Every migration is additive, so the old process keeps working against the new schema between steps 4 and 8.
  • Avoid restarting at 04:00-04:35 (nightly sync and Insights), 06:30 / 12:30 / 17:30 / 22:30 (sales re-pulls), 09:00 (Morning summary), 10:00 (lead tasks) and 21:30 (closing-checklist push).
  • Rollback (light): git reset --hard <previous>, keep the DB (old code ignores new tables/columns), swap dist-prev back, kickstart. Optional alembic downgrade. Full restore from the .bak-pre-* copy only for a damaged DB (loses later writes).
  • App releases are separate: Xcode archive of the Flutter app, TestFlight, App Store review. The server always stays compatible with app builds 5-9 already installed (additive API only).

2.6 Backups, logs and disk

ItemState
Database backupsManual only: an online sqlite3 .backup (spicetown.db.bak-pre-NNNN-<ts>) before every migration, kept next to the DB. No scheduled backup and no off-machine copy exists.
Logsbackend/logs/backend.log, backend.error.log (Python logging goes to stderr), cloudflared and watchdog logs. No rotation configured.

2.7 Python environments and the dev server

  • .venv312 (Python 3.12) is the live production venv. .venv (Python 3.9) is kept for rollback and for the dev test runs - code must stay 3.9-compatible (typing.Optional, never X | None).
  • Dev: ~/spicetown-dev/up.sh / down.sh (PID file, never touches prod). Dev .env sets SCHEDULER_ENABLED, NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED and TEAM_JOBS_ENABLED to false so dev never spends the shared Toast rate limit or sends anything.
  • Throwaway test servers (regression suites) run on other ports over a .backup copy of prod with every outside service blank, and are killed afterwards.

3 Security and access

3.1 Authentication

There is one user table and one session table for both clients. A session is an opaque random token (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)) stored as the primary key of user_sessions with a 14-day expiry (SESSION_LIFETIME_DAYS). Passwords are bcrypt hashes. There are no JWTs: deleting the row revokes a session at once (an admin password reset deletes every session of that user). There is no 'forgot password' - only an admin sets a password; anyone can change their own with the current one.

WebsiteMobile appLabels app

3.5 Demo guard (App Review login)

The App Review login must be able to look around but never change real data or reach anyone. app/demo_guard.py is an app-wide FastAPI dependency: for a demo session every POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE is refused with 403 DEMO_READ_ONLY unless its (method, path) is on an allowlist of 50 entries, some with an ownership check. New routes are refused by default; tests/test_demo_guard.py enumerates app.routes to keep it that way. Every Oct 15 write route (steps editing, bulk, prefs reset, store defaults) is deliberately not on the list.

3.6 Public links, invoice links and HTTP security headers

  • Public checklist link {PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/c/<slug>-<4-digit code> plus a 22-character token for the API. An admin turns it on per checklist, optionally with a list of allowed names and a per-hour cap (default 6, max 60); rotate gives a new code. It reaches exactly one checklist's form, submit and photo upload.
  • Page response headers: Cache-Control: no-store, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY and CSP default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' blob: data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self' data:; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'. The 'not active' page uses default-src 'none'.
  • Invoice links (/public/invoices/{token}) used to be public-by-unguessable-token; they now need a dashboard login (feature invoice_submission). A logged-out tap is redirected to /#/login?next=....
  • Team media (/api/team/media/{token}) and flyer files need a login and pass an owner-specific access check (task readers, channel members, announcement recipients).
  • The main website sets no CSP of its own; it is same-origin and loads no third-party scripts.

3.8 Known security gaps and decisions

  • No login throttling or lockout on the two login routes, although they are on the public internet.
  • One SQLite file on one machine; backups are manual and on the same disk.
  • No log rotation; logs can contain usernames, vendor names and push titles (never passwords, tokens or push bodies).
  • Admin is all-or-nothing (no partial admin).
  • The labels app trusts the dashboard session table directly (read-only); revoking a dashboard session also revokes labels access.

4 Data model

One SQLite database, 58 tables declared in the models plus alembic_version. Models live in app/models.py and in small per-feature files (insights_models.py, issue_lead_models.py, po_send_models.py, setting_models.py, notification_models.py, team/models.py, team/tasks_models.py, team/chat_models.py).

  • Conventions: every timestamp column is UTCDateTime (stored UTC, UTC re-attached on read); business dates are plain dates in store time (America/New_York).
  • Name snapshots: 'by' columns keep a name next to the user id (created_by_name, placed_by_name...), so history reads correctly after an account is deleted.
  • Few hard foreign keys: most links are logical (vendor names, item ids, checklist types, issue keys). In the diagrams a solid line is a real FOREIGN KEY, a dotted line a logical link the code follows.
  • Toast identity: orders.item_guid = inventory_snapshots.item_id = toast_menu_items.item_id (the Toast menu item GUID).
  • Row counts below are from a read-only query of production on the day this was written (production was at 0056, so push_deliveries does not exist there yet).

5.4 Scheduled jobs

Three APScheduler BackgroundSchedulers inside the backend process, all in America/New_York. Each has its own kill switch so the dev server can run the safe ones. Most jobs use coalesce=True and max_instances=1 so a slow run never stacks.

6 Website

6.1 Stack and entry points

  • React 18 + Vite 5 + react-router-dom 7 (HashRouter), plain CSS (index.css + a few per-page files). No global state library; each page holds its own state.
  • main.jsx: for /c/ paths renders only PublicChecklistPage; otherwise App.jsx: AuthProvider → GlossaryProvider → HashRouter → AppShell (Sidebar + routes + floating CartButton + Ask-bot ChatWidget).
  • src/api.js (about 2,050 lines): one exported function per endpoint. request() sends credentials: 'include' (the session cookie), turns a non-2xx answer into an Error with status and body, and on any 401 (except login) dispatches auth:unauthorized, which sends the user to the login page. Uploads with progress use XMLHttpRequest.
  • AuthContext loads GET /api/auth/me once: hasFeature(key) (admins: true; Items Sold false for hide_sales), canSeeSales, user.demo.
  • src/featureRoutes.js is the single source for which route needs which feature, the landing page order and the sidebar (NAV_GROUPS, buildSidebar, routeVisible, footerLinks). A group with exactly one visible link renders as that plain link.
  • Legacy: @capacitor/* packages, mobileAuth.js and a build:mobile script remain from the retired Capacitor wrapper; the Flutter app replaced it.

6.5 State and sync patterns

PatternWhereHow
Load on mount + manual refreshMost pagesuseEffect calls api.js, local useState; buttons re-fetch. No client cache beyond the page.
Team change feed (one shared loop)useTeamSync / teamSyncEngine.js: sidebar badges, Tasks page, task drawerOne cursor loop for the whole site. While the Tasks page or a drawer is open: long-poll GET /api/team/updates?since=&wait=20&include=tasks. Other pages: badge poll every badge_poll_interval_s (120 s) with wait=0. Hidden tab asks nothing, then once when shown. Errors back off 2 s .. 60 s. An empty answer under 1.5 s twice = older server, plain polling.
Patch from the feedTasks page, drawerRows in the feed's tasks[] are patched at once; a changes.task entry triggers a debounced (250 ms) reload; changes.team reloads bootstrap (member counts).
Write answers applied directlyTask drawerEvery task write returns task_out; the drawer shows it without another GET. A 409 carries the current task, shown with the error.
Chat pollingTeamChatPageChange-feed tick every 5-10 s; open conversation polls messages every chat_poll_interval_s (5 s).
AnnouncementsTeamAnnouncementsPageInterval of poll_interval_s (30 s).
Job statusOverview JobStatusWidgetGET /api/jobs/status every 60 s.
Flyer send statusFlyerDrawer / SendFlyerModalGET /api/flyers/{id} every 3 s while a send is waiting or going.
Invoice statusInvoicesGET /api/invoices/{id} after submit until WhatsApp / email settle.
Insights stalenessinsightsModel.staleTextShows the server's note (why a day is missing and when it arrives).

7 Mobile app

7.1 Stack, start-up and the update gate

  • Flutter (Dart 3), Riverpod 2 (state), go_router 16 (routes), Dio 5 (HTTP). Version 2.0.0+8 in pubspec (the build number is bumped only at release). iOS 15.5+, bundle com.spicetown.app; Android package the same.
  • main.dart → bootstrap() (ProviderScope + FreshnessObserver for resume) → SpicetownApp → UpdateGate wrapping the router.
  • UpdateGate: GET /api/app/config (no login) gives min_supported_build_ios / _android and store URLs; a build below the minimum gets a blocking 'Update required' screen. Checked at launch and on every return to the foreground; a failed check never blocks. Both minimums are 0 (never block) today.
  • Router redirect enforces the session life cycle: bootstrapping → /splash, unauthenticated → /login, authenticated → /home.
  • API base: --dart-define API_BASE_URL (default https://ops.spicetown.shop) and LABELS_BASE_URL (default https://labels.spicetown.shop).

7.2 Tabs and screens

A StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack keeps five branch navigators (each tab keeps its own stack). Most detail screens are pushed with MaterialPageRoute from tiles; every tile and search result comes from one featureIndex (title, access rule, destination), so Store, More › Setup and search can never disagree about who may open what. Old paths redirect (/orders, /reports, /ordering → /store; /more/insights → /store/insights; /more/flyers → Team › Flyers).

7.3 Layers inside the app

SettingValue
Timeoutsconnect 15 s, receive 30 s, send 45 s; Ask bot receive 120 s; open-checks rescan 5 min
HeadersAuthorization: Bearer <token>; X-Client-Tab-Names: 1 (server sends tab names for open checks)
ErrorsApiException with the server's detail; 401 (except credential paths) signs out; no automatic retry
OfflineConnectivityInterceptor flips an offline banner on network errors and pings /api/health every 8 s until back. No offline data store: lists keep their last in-memory value; the glossary is bundled.

7.5 Push notifications and deep links

  • Registration: after sign-in the app asks permission once (answer remembered), gets the FCM token and calls POST /api/notifications/devices {token, platform}; the last registered token is remembered so it is sent again only when it changes. Sign-out calls DELETE /api/notifications/devices; if that fails, the token is kept as 'pending unregister' and sent to the open POST /api/notifications/unregister later.
  • Payload: data values are strings: type (the alert key), route, and optional vendor, invoice_id, horizon_days, task_id, channel_id, message_id, announcement_id, report_id, flyer_id, insights page. An unknown route (older build, new route) opens Home.
  • Routes understood: supplier_projection (needs vendor), delivery_review, checklists, reorder, invoice, open_orders, task (needs task_id), chat (needs channel_id), announcement (needs announcement_id), moderation, fix_issues / issues, cart / purchase_cart, flyers / flyer, inventory_api(_ready), loss_watch / odd_checks, insights*, home; and by type when the route is unknown: fix_issues_reopened, cart_removal_request, flyer_sent, inventory_api_ready, loss_watch.
  • Foreground: notifications are shown while the app is open; a push arriving in the foreground triggers an immediate Team poll (Oct 15).
  • Task action.route uses the same route names, so a task's main button opens the real work screen in every build.

7.9 iPad layout

  • Content is centred at a maximum width of 720 px (ContentWidthLimit); the login form at 480 px.
  • Device-matrix widget tests cover 10 shapes (iPhone SE at 1x and 2x text, standard phones, iPad portrait and Split View 507 px) for overflow and reachability.
  • The Oct 15 regression fixed one iPad issue: Store defaults rows were each centred to their own width.

7.10 Demo mode in the app

  • /api/auth/me returns demo: true; a DemoAccountNote explains that sends are off.
  • Hidden for the demo: More › Setup, Flyers, Reset to recommended, Store defaults, bulk task actions, 'My team today', step editing, Critical actions, Vendor contacts.
  • Everything the App Review notes ask the reviewer to try still works: Home › Upload Invoice (saved, never sent), Home › Daily Checklists (saved, never sent to WhatsApp), Team (tasks and chat inside its Review team), More › Delete my account (refused with a clear message for the demo), More › About.

8 End-to-end flows

Each flow below follows one function from the person's tap to the database, the outside systems and back, and names what other screens see afterwards. Paths are relative to https://ops.spicetown.shop; W = website, A = app.

8.1 Sign in (website)

  • Landing page: firstAccessiblePath walks FEATURE_ROUTES in order (Overview first) and picks the first granted, non-retired page; nothing granted = /no-access.
  • Admin actions that end sessions: set-password and delete user delete every user_sessions row of that user; their next request gets 401 and both clients return to login.

8.2 Sales sync, accuracy re-pull and live 'today'

  • Accuracy: at 06:30, 12:30, 17:30 and 22:30 sales_accuracy.run_sales_repull asks Toast Analytics for each of the last 14 days' totals, compares them with orders, and re-syncs only the dates that differ (Toast keeps editing closed days: voids, discounts, late payments). Admins see the result on Items Sold (GET /api/sales/accuracy, POST /api/sales/accuracy/run).
  • Today is never stored: Items Sold 'today' and Overview's sales tile pull Toast live through items_sold.py (one call, shared for 60 s by every page asking).
  • Revenue rule: a sale counts on its payment date (paid_at), not when it was opened; modifiers count inside their parent.
  • Consumers: Items Sold, forecast / reorder / projection (through the report cache), Fix Issues 'last sold', weekly digest, Insights compare, delivery suggestions, reconciliation.

8.3 Inventory upload (Toast CSV / XLSX)

8.4 Inventory from Toast (04:05 snapshot, comparison, switch, live stock)

  • Switch: admins flip 'Use Toast for inventory' on the Inventory from Toast page (PUT /api/inventory-api/switch); stored with history in setting_changes; effective at once. INVENTORY_API_SNAPSHOTS is only its starting value.
  • Live stock overlay (switch on): Supplier Projection, Reorder and Fix Issues read Toast's current on-hand on top of the latest snapshot (cached 300 s; a refresh ends the report cache).
  • Hourly menu re-check: metadata first, full menu only if lastUpdated changed -> toast_menu_items (barcodes for search and Fix Issues).
  • Compare now (GET /api/inventory-api/compare?refresh=1, once per 120 s) builds the Toast set in memory; it never writes inventory.

8.5 Forecast, Reorder Candidates and Supplier Projection

8.6 Home Today card (app)

TileSourceActions from the tile
My tasksTeam change feed + GET /api/team/tasks (mine, open, due today / overdue)Open task; complete
Orders dueGET /api/vendor-calendar?start=today&end=tomorrow (report cache counts)Sheet: Order already placed, Skip this week, Other, Undo -> POST / DELETE /api/order-actions (admins)
CriticalGET /api/ordering/reorder-candidates?lookback=30&lead=7&critical_only=1, kept 10 minSheet: Close, Skip this week, Remind me later (POST /api/reorder/critical-dismissals), Order already placed; Show again
Open checksGET /api/orders/open (today)Open Open Checks
InvoicesGET /api/invoices (failed sends, and sent invoices not yet closed in Toast, using each row's close_suggested flag)Resend; Close in Toast
ChecklistsGET /api/checklists/schemas + GET /api/checklists (today) after the due timeOpen the checklist form
  • Pull-to-refresh / Refresh all keep the two heavy reports (Critical, Orders due) if they loaded under 2 minutes ago; a failed load is always asked again.
  • Order actions apply on the phone at once (local changes provider); 'Order already placed' from the Critical sheet marks the vendor's next order-due in place without reloading the calendar (Oct 15).
  • The website shows the same information on Overview (stat tiles, Today's schedule) and on Reorder / Vendor Calendar.

8.7 Critical vendors: Skip this week / Remind me later / Close

8.8 Vendor calendar, order actions and schedule suggestions

  • Schedule suggestions: GET /api/vendor-calendar/schedule-suggestions infers weekdays from invoices, placed orders, the purchase log, snapshots and Toast receipts, with a confidence, and lists vendors without a schedule; Accept / Edit / Dismiss, or Add all (POST .../accept-all). It never changes a schedule by itself.
  • Vendors have minimum orders: an order-due with fewer than 5 items needing order is not urgent (same rule as Reorder's VENDOR_MIN_ORDER_ITEMS).
  • Consumers: Home Orders due, the Morning summary's 'Order today / tomorrow' line, the (off) order auto-task rule, Reorder's 'already ordered'.

8.9 PO cart -> PDF -> Send PO (email + CC, WhatsApp) -> Placed orders

  • Removal: admins delete a line; staff request removal (POST /cart/items/{id}/removal-request), admins approve / reject; the 10-minute cart_removal_request push tells admins.
  • History: GET /api/ordering/orders (Placed Orders), POST /orders/{id}/order-again puts lines back in the cart. Home shows the 3 latest (Recent orders).
  • PO sections: automatic from category (with category_overrides), edited on PO sections (/api/categories/*, item / vendor / rename rules); the cart preview shows the effect.
  • Cart with projection context (GET /cart?projection=1, about 1 s): the app re-reads it only when a line is added / removed / re-cased or a shared item's qty changes (2 s debounce).

8.10 Deliveries, reconciliation and transfers

  • Reconciliation: expected_closing = opening + purchased - sold; variance = counted - expected (shrinkage / unlogged purchases). Purchase log by form, CSV/XLSX import, or Delivery Review. 'Invoices without a logged purchase' compares invoices with the log by vendor and date. Worked example lives in Help.
  • Transfers (Store <-> Container): the page is retired (redirects to Delivery Review); /api/transfers/* and location_transfers stay for old app builds.

8.11 Invoice scan -> submit -> WhatsApp + Toast email -> close

  • Failures: the 10-minute invoice_failed alert goes to the submitter and admins; Resend (POST /{id}/resend) retries; admins can override a status. Ambiguous WhatsApp timeouts are reconciled against the chat history.
  • Closed in Toast: invoice_close_suggestions spots the receiving in Toast and suggests the tap; a person marks it (POST /{id}/mark-toast-closed), which also closes any invoice auto task (source_sync 'invoice').
  • Delete: request-delete -> admin approve-delete -> trash -> restore or permanent delete. Invoice links need a login.
  • Website: Invoices page (list, statuses, Resend, close, delete workflow, trash). Overview pre-fills 'we received a delivery today' from today's invoice vendors.

8.12 Labels

The labels catalog is a CSV built by a GitHub Action from Toast, pulled every 15 minutes (com.spicetown.labels.sync); price changes can auto-print. The website links to the labels app (Label Scanner in the footer); Home's 'Print labels' and Scan's History icon open Print Label History.

8.13 Fix Issues, leads and the daily lead tasks

  • Lists: missing barcodes, invalid barcodes (GS1 check digit), duplicates, dead stock (with / without stock), slow review, negative inventory, refill from container. 'More time' snoozes for a week; at 09:00 the ended snoozes come back (a Morning summary line, opt-in push).
  • Leads (admin page /api/issue-leads): who leads each PO section, vendor, and the fallback. Settings: daily time (default 10:00), hours until due (default 6, per lead or per type).
  • Daily lead task: inside the 5-minute task job, after the set time, run_issue_lead_rule creates one task per lead with that morning's list (issue_lead_task_runs.items_json = M) and sends 'New task' only (its due / overdue reminders are governed by the opt-in fix_issues_task_due). The task's action opens that lead's Fix Issues list.
  • Items that drop off by themselves (fixed in Toast + new upload, no Fix Issues close) count at the next morning's run.

8.14 Daily checklists, public links and WhatsApp groups

  • Builder (admins, website and app): Google-Forms-like editor; draft (PUT), publish creates an immutable version, revert, duplicate, order. Old app build 5 still gets LEGACY blocks it can render.
  • Public link: admin turns it on per checklist (PUT .../public-link), rotates the code, sets allowed names and the hourly cap. Guards in section 3.6.
  • WhatsApp groups (admins): register Whapi groups by key (/api/checklists/admin/whatsapp-groups), list available groups (Whapi GET /groups, cached 5 min), mark marketing groups for flyers.
  • Closing-checklist tasks are no longer created (Oct 15: TEAM_AUTOTASK_CHECKLIST_ENABLED default false); leftovers are closed by the task job as cancelled 'Missed - not submitted' (never tasks 11, 12, 47 or the Review team's).

8.15 Team tasks: create, assign, sync, complete

Task writeRouteNotes
EditPATCH /api/team/tasks/{id}Only changed fields + optional expected_updated_at; mismatch = 409 with the current task
StepsPATCH .../items/{item_id} (tick / rename), POST .../items, PUT .../items (whole list), DELETE .../items/{item_id}Max 30 steps; creator / admin edit, assignees tick; events item_done, item_undone, items_edited
Can't do / start / reopen / commentPOST .../cant-do, /start, /reopen, /commentscan't do pushes the creator and admins (on by default)
ReportPOST .../report, .../comments/{id}/reportInto the moderation queue
Bulk (admins)POST /api/team/tasks/bulk {task_ids, action done or cancel}Max 200; skips photo-required and closed tasks
Batch cancelPOST /api/team/task-batches/{id}/cancelCancel every copy of a multi-person assignment
SummaryGET /api/team/task-summary'My team today': admins everyone, can_assign their teams; demo 403
FiltersGET /api/team/tasks?assignee_user_id&source&q&statusNarrow the view, never widen it
  • Who sees a task: the assignee (or every current member of the assigned team), the creator, admins. A team task is one row any member can complete (first one wins); several named people = one row each.
  • Badges: tasks_due = open tasks for me or my teams due by the end of today (overdue included), returned with every change-feed answer.
  • Pushes: task_assigned (on), task_cant_do (on), task_due overdue for your own tasks (on), 'Due in 30 minutes' (task_due_soon, off), lead task reminders (fix_issues_task_due, off), task_done and task_comment (off). The 5-minute sweep only targets people who can receive it, and logs a no-recipient push once so it is never rebuilt.

8.16 Recurring schedules (website and app)

DST: a local time that does not exist (spring forward) moves to the next valid time; a repeated hour is used once. Deleting a template deactivates it (history keeps its tasks).

8.17 Automatic tasks and source sync

Rule (TEAM_AUTOTASK_*)DefaultCreatesClosed by
checklistOFF since Oct 15(none) - leftovers closed as 'Missed - not submitted'checklist submit (source_sync 'checklist')
invoiceoff'Resend / fix invoice' when sends failedmark-toast-closed / approve-delete / delete ('invoice')
orderoff'Place the order' for an order-due vendor with >= 5 itemsorder actions, mark-placed, Critical skip_week ('order'); expires after 7 days
issue_leadson (leads configured)One Fix Issues task per lead per dayFix Issues close / reopen ('issue_leads') -> progress, closes at 0

team/source_sync.task_sources_changed(kind) runs the cheap 'close' half of a rule right after the source's own commit, in its own short session, and never raises; the 5-minute job stays the safety net. Every system close is a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status='open', so it can never overwrite a person's done or can't do. Protected: tasks 11, 12, 47 and anything of a demo login or its teams.

8.18 Chat

Channels: one per team (membership derived live from team_members) plus DMs (POST /channels/dm, dm_key). Also: pins, seen-by, search, mute / hide per channel, DM blocks, delete own message (soft; text kept 30 days for moderation), chat settings 'hide message text' in pushes. Retention: 365 days. The demo login only sees people sharing a team with it.

8.19 Announcements (News)

8.20 Moderation

Anyone in a channel can report a message; anyone who can see a task can report it or a comment (message_reports with a snapshot). Admins see one queue (GET /api/team/reports, website Setup › Reported messages, app More › Setup) and resolve (optionally removing the content) or dismiss. The content filter masks objectionable words in chat, task text, comments and announcements (first letter kept), never rejects them. Team rules (EULA) must be accepted once before Team opens (POST /api/team/rules/accept, versioned).

  • Settings API: GET/PUT /api/notifications/prefs (items grouped, with default, essential, admin_only, explicit), POST /prefs/reset (own catalog rows only), GET /recent; admins: GET/PUT /defaults, POST /defaults/reset, GET /volume?days=14. 8.22 Marketing flyers

8.23 Insights (Toast Analytics): two-step reports, cache, budget, catch-up

ReportKept (days)Used by
metrics_day91Daily compare (and 4-week average), check trends, weekly digest, Morning summary sales line
metrics_dining84Sales channels
metrics_hour84Busy hours heatmap, prep forecast
menu_item112Menu trends, best and worst sellers
menu_modifier56Add-ons
check (daily budget 30)30Loss watch, Odd checks (admins)
guest payments (daily budget 10)84Returning customers (card fingerprints stored only as an HMAC)
  • Nightly 04:30: yesterday's reports, re-pulls of the last 14 days (check: 7), some older history within per-report call caps, the menu map, then Loss watch / Odd checks flags; purge (guest 400 days, check 120, cache 400, call log 7). Job status: success / partial (budget) / failed, with warnings.
  • Reserve: the last 2 closed days always come first; older days only spend what is above the reserve (check 4, guest 2), so a backfill or a hand-run can't leave the newest day waiting 24 h.
  • Catch-up: hourly at :20 from 05:20 to 23:20; reads the cache first and calls Toast only for a missing newest day while the budget has room.
  • Unavailable: Toast answering 404/409 repeatedly marks the date unavailable (not a $0 day); the nightly retries it once a night.
  • Access: feature sales_insights; Loss watch and Odd checks admin only; hide_sales gets counts only (heatmap) or 403 for sales-only pages.

8.24 Ask Inventory Bot

8.25 Weekly digest

Overview › Weekly Digest (kept by the owner): POST /api/weekly-digest/generate gathers the trailing 7 days from the existing services (reorder, dead stock, vendor price comparison, reconciliation, barcode quality, sales vs the prior week - left out for hide_sales) and makes one claude-opus-5 call to write the narrative. Generated on demand, not stored. Demo: canned text.

D Appendix D - Client calls checked against the server

Every endpoint the website (api.js through its pages) and the app (repositories) call was matched against the server's routes. 281 distinct client calls; every one matches a server route (method and path).

Server routes no client page or repository references (33): kept for old app builds, used by the public checklist page, by scripts, or reached through a helper the analyser does not follow: file and image URLs used directly in links / img tags, CSV downloads, and the app's core calls outside repositories (/api/health connectivity ping, /api/app/config update gate, /api/glossary).
